items.locator: StatPearls Barrett Esophagus — Etiology/Risk Factors and clinical overview: chronic gastroesophageal reflux disease is a major precipitating/risk factor for Barrett esophagus, in which distal esophageal epithelium undergoes intestinal metaplasia and carries increased adenocarcinoma risk.
items.version: StatPearls Barrett Esophagus updated 2025-05-26 and available in StatPearls [Internet] 2026; NCBI source live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.source_name: KDIGO — 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
items.locator: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline, Definition and Classification of CKD, Kidney International 105(Suppl 4S), p. S137: classify CKD based on Cause, GFR category (G1-G5), and Albuminuria category (A1-A3), abbreviated CGA.
items.version: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline remains the current global CKD guideline; KDIGO notes a focused update of Chapter 3 is underway. Currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. Blueprint corrected to Reduction of Risk Potential because the item tests diagnostic/laboratory-based CKD classification.

items.locator: StatPearls Myxedema Coma — History and Physical/Evaluation: decompensated severe hypothyroidism typically features altered mental status and hypothermia, with bradycardia, hypotension/hypoventilation and multisystem dysfunction; it is a life-threatening endocrine emergency.
items.version: StatPearls Myxedema Coma updated 2025-12-13 and current in StatPearls [Internet] 2026; NCBI source live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline — Primary Adrenal Insufficiency, clinical features/diagnostic considerations: glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid deficiency can cause fatigue/weakness, volume depletion and hypotension, salt craving, and hyperpigmentation from elevated ACTH in primary disease.
items.version: Endocrine Society Primary Adrenal Insufficiency guideline remains the current society guideline resource; live source and current status rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: StatPearls Hypokalemia — Etiology/Clinical Features/ECG: loop diuretics can cause renal potassium loss; serum potassium below 3.5 mEq/L is hypokalemia, and levels around 2.5-3.0 mEq/L may cause muscle weakness and decreased gastrointestinal motility/constipation; ECG changes include T-wave flattening/depression and U waves.
items.version: Current StatPearls Hypokalemia entry in StatPearls [Internet] 2026; NCBI source live-rechecked 2026-08-15. Blueprint corrected from Physiological Adaptation to Reduction of Risk Potential because the item primarily tests laboratory/ECG interpretation and medication-related risk.

items.locator: Endotext Hyperglycemic Crises — Diagnostic criteria/clinical manifestations of DKA: metabolic acidosis is reflected by pH <7.3 and/or serum bicarbonate <18 mmol/L; Kussmaul respiration is deep, labored/rapid breathing that compensates for metabolic acidosis.
items.version: Endotext Hyperglycemic Crises updated 2026-01-31; current NCBI Bookshelf version live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.source_name: StatPearls/NCBI Bookshelf — Chronic Kidney Disease-Mineral Bone Disorder
items.locator: StatPearls CKD-Mineral Bone Disorder — Pathophysiology: declining kidney function impairs phosphate excretion and calcitriol production, contributing to hyperphosphatemia, lower serum calcium/hypocalcemia, and secondary hyperparathyroidism in advanced CKD.
items.version: Current StatPearls CKD-MBD entry in StatPearls [Internet] 2026; NCBI source live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: StatPearls Neutrophilia — Etiology, Infection/Inflammation: infection and inflammation are common causes of reactive neutrophilia; bacterial infections are usually associated with a left shift, meaning increased band/immature neutrophil forms. The differential must be interpreted with the clinical presentation rather than treated as diagnostic alone.
items.version: StatPearls Neutrophilia, StatPearls [Internet] 2026; NCBI source live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.rationale: Neutrophilia can occur with infection and inflammation, and bacterial infections commonly produce a left shift with increased immature neutrophil forms. In a client with fever and productive cough, that pattern increases concern for an acute bacterial respiratory infection, but the CBC differential does not establish the diagnosis by itself. Option A appropriately integrates the laboratory pattern with the clinical presentation. Options B and C misstate the association, and Option D incorrectly ignores clinically relevant abnormalities.

items.locator: National Cancer Institute — Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) Test Fact Sheet: PSA is produced by normal and malignant prostate cells; levels can rise with prostate cancer but also with benign prostatic hyperplasia, prostatitis/inflammation, and other factors, so an elevated PSA alone does not diagnose prostate cancer.
items.version: Current NCI PSA Fact Sheet live-rechecked 2026-08-15; difficulty corrected to easy because the item tests direct interpretation of a nonspecific tumor marker rather than multistep clinical judgment.

items.locator: National Cancer Institute — Ovarian Cancer Screening (PDQ), CA-125: CA-125 is associated with ovarian cancer but lacks diagnostic specificity; elevated values can occur in benign gynecologic/non-gynecologic conditions and other malignancies, so the result cannot diagnose ovarian cancer by itself.
items.version: Current NCI Ovarian Cancer Screening PDQ live-rechecked 2026-08-15; difficulty corrected to easy because the item tests direct nonspecific-marker interpretation.
